chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadijah, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Do not give from the zakat anyone whom you support."

And he said: If a man has five hundred dirhams and his dependents are many, he said: "There is no zakat upon him; he spends it on his dependents, increasing their maintenance, their clothing, and the food they did not previously eat."
And if he has no dependents and is alone, let him divide it among people who are not needy, who are proud of asking, who do not ask anyone for anything."
And he said: "Do not give your relatives all the zakat, but give them some and divide the rest among the other Muslims."

And he said: "Zakat is permissible for the head of the house and the servant, and for anyone who has five hundred dirhams after having dependents, and he makes the zakat of the five hundred an increase in the maintenance of his dependents, expanding their provision."
ai.seo_question: Can I give my own zakat to my family members?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying the Shia juristic view that a payer may give zakat to his own dependents, treating it as an enhancement of their maintenance (*nafaqa*) rather than a separate gift. This ruling distinguishes between the obligation of general sustenance and the specific purifying wealth of zakat, while also establishing that relatives should receive only a portion to avoid the appearance of merely redistributing one's own funds within the family unit.
